## Overview {#sec-overview}

Give a brief a description of your project and its goal(s), what data you are using to complete it, and what two faculty/staff in different fields you have spoken to about your project with a brief summary of what you learned from each person. Include a link to your final project GitHub repository.

**This project examines how neighborhood walkability relates to the geographic distribution of diabetes and depression prevalence across US counties. Using CDC PLACES 2025, the EPA National Walkability Index, and US Census county boundaries, I will explore geographic patterns and associations through statistical analysis, data visualization, and mapping.**

## Introduction {#sec-introduction}

Describe the problem addressed, its significance, and some background to motivate the problem. This should extend what is in the @sec-overview.

Explain why your problem is interdisciplinary, what fields can contribute to its understanding, and incorporate background related to what you learned from meeting with faculty/staff.

**Diabetes and depression are major chronic conditions that can affect individuals' health and quality of life. Neighborhood walkability may influence health through opportunities for physical activity and access to healthcare. Therefore, the relationship between walkability and the geographic distribution of these two conditions may be worth investigating. The project aims to investigate these patterns across US counties and identify the correlation between relatively high prevalence of both conditions and poor walkability.**

**This project needs an interdisciplinary approach because it combines clinical understanding, public health perspectives, epidemiology, and geographic data science. Especially, public health perspectives provide a strategy for understanding population-level health differences related to zip code.**
